subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Calcium is an important mineral for performers because it:
questions.explain: Calcium is needed for strong bones and teeth, reducing the risk of fractures.

questions.q: The principle that fitness gains are lost when training stops is known as:
questions.explain: Reversibility means fitness levels decline if training is stopped or reduced.

questions.q: What do the letters FITT stand for?
questions.explain: FITT stands for Frequency, Intensity, Time and Type - principles used to apply overload.

questions.q: Which training method involves explosive bounding, hopping and jumping to develop power?
questions.explain: Plyometric training uses explosive movements to develop muscular power.

questions.q: Which is a likely consequence of a sedentary lifestyle?
options: Increased risk of obesity and heart disease
questions.explain: A sedentary lifestyle increases the risk of obesity, high blood pressure and coronary heart disease.

questions.q: Obesity is best defined as:
options: Having a large amount of muscle
Having excess body fat to the extent that health may be affected
questions.explain: Obesity is an excessive accumulation of body fat that may negatively affect health.

questions.q: The ruler drop test is used to measure:
questions.explain: The ruler drop test measures reaction time by recording how far a ruler falls before it is caught.

questions.q: The vertical jump test (Sargent jump) is used to measure which component of fitness?
questions.explain: The vertical jump test measures explosive leg power.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes health and fitness?
options: They mean exactly the same thing
Health is a state of complete well-being; fitness is the ability to meet the demands of the environment
Health only refers to physical strength
Fitness includes mental health but health does not
questions.explain: Health is complete physical, mental and social well-being, while fitness is the ability to cope with the demands of activity.

questions.q: Iron is an important mineral in the diet because it:
options: Helps form haemoglobin to carry oxygen
questions.explain: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin in red blood cells, which transports oxygen.

questions.q: Using the formula 220 - age, what is the maximum heart rate of a 16-year-old?
questions.explain: Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 - age, so 220 - 16 = 204 bpm.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of emotional health and well-being?
options: Having a strong heart and lungs
Making friends through a sports team
Being able to control emotions and feel relaxed
questions.explain: Emotional well-being relates to managing emotions, feeling confident and reducing stress.

questions.q: Which somatotype is muscular and broad-shouldered, often suited to power sports?
questions.explain: Mesomorphs are muscular, broad-shouldered and well suited to strength and power events.

questions.q: Which component of fitness is the ability of a muscle to repeatedly contract over time without tiring?
questions.explain: Muscular endurance is the ability of a muscle or muscle group to keep contracting against a resistance over time.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a cool-down after exercise?
options: To gradually lower heart rate and remove waste products
questions.explain: A cool-down gradually lowers heart rate and helps remove lactic acid, reducing stiffness.

questions.q: Which component of fitness is the ability to move the whole body quickly and change direction?
questions.explain: Agility is the ability to change direction quickly while keeping control of the body.

questions.q: Fartlek training is best described as:
options: Short maximal sprints with full rest
Training at a constant steady pace
questions.explain: Fartlek, meaning 'speed play', varies intensity and terrain, developing both aerobic and anaerobic fitness.

questions.q: The sit-and-reach test is used to measure:
questions.explain: The sit-and-reach test measures flexibility, particularly of the lower back and hamstrings.

questions.q: Which macronutrient is the body's main source of energy, especially for high-intensity exercise?
questions.explain: Carbohydrates are the body's main and most readily available energy source.

questions.q: A key reason for performing a warm-up before exercise is to:
options: Increase muscle temperature and reduce injury risk
questions.explain: A warm-up raises muscle temperature and prepares the body, reducing the risk of injury.

questions.q: Which performer is most likely to benefit from an endomorph somatotype?
questions.explain: Endomorphs carry more body mass, which can be an advantage in sports such as sumo wrestling.

questions.q: Which somatotype would generally be the greatest advantage for a long-distance runner?
questions.explain: An ectomorph's light, lean build is well suited to endurance events such as long-distance running.
